source.dataset: MIT Election Data and Science Lab (MEDSL), U.S. House constituency returns 1976-2018
source.also_published_at: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/IG0UN2 (there the file is behind a guestbook and cannot be fetched unattended)
source.upstream_source: Clerk of the U.S. House, "Statistics of the Congressional Election"; 2018 from state election offices

transform: Keep stage="gen" and special=FALSE. Group candidate rows by year+state+district.
Sum candidatevotes across party lines for the same candidate name (NY/CT fusion), name upper-cased and stripped to A-Z and spaces.
Label a candidate D if any of its lines is democrat / democratic-farmer-labor / democratic-npl, R if republican, otherwise other and excluded from the two-party totals.

inc: +1 if the top D candidate won any seat in the same state two years earlier, -1 if the top R did, 0 if neither or both. State-wide matching absorbs redistricting and district-hopping; special-election winners are missed.
